bull_case_summary: Broadcom has $13.665bn quarterly FCF, 171% GAAP operating-income growth and actual debt reduction to $59.419bn. Round two uses 20.51x interest coverage and measured debt progress to defend manageability and growth participation at estimated 19.38x earnings.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts a credible purchase thesis and financing evidence. Its case narrows to customer concentration, recurring SBC and $35.444bn net debt becoming more sensitive if demand slows, rather than treating future uncertainty as a veto.
key_points_of_agreement: Cash and GAAP growth validate economics beyond adjusted earnings.
Actual debt repayment is stronger evidence than annualising one quarter.
Guidance and forward earnings remain prospective.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far measured manageability and growth compensate concentration and valuation sensitivity.
unresolved_uncertainties: Future concentrated customer demand and trade-policy effects.
Delivery of forecast earnings without capitalising exceptional quarterly cash as permanent.
